extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, grant applicants, institutional research administrators, and reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page that summarizes recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and guidance relevant to grant applicants, reviewers, and administrators. Includes pointers to new formats, initiatives, and explanations of review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate research models
rubrics_metrics.description: "Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential; however, choice of model should be driven by fit to the specific research question rather than trend or novelty alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare DMS Plans using the new simplified required elements in the 2026 pilot format — consult the new resource for the exact elements and formatting expectations when submitting applications that require DMS Plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout research
rubrics_metrics.description: "Embedding Replication and Reproducibility Throughout NIH Research: Key Reminders for Applications, Awards, and a New Highlighted Topic" and "NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH encourages applicants and awardees to plan for and prioritize replication and reproducibility; the new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative aims to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize these efforts across the biomedical research enterprise. Address replication/reproducibility explicitly where relevant in applications and plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the 'Competitive but Not Discussed' review designation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of NIH review triaging practices: applications can be scored as competitive yet not discussed in full panel discussion (middle third). This affects interpretation of summary statements and next steps for applicants (e.g., resubmission strategy, administrative queries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PF5 Collaborative International Research Project application features
rubrics_metrics.description: "New Video Overview for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) — Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview ... to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants to PF5 should learn key features and the specific application format (watch the short overview). Be aware that, after review and prior to Just-in-Time, applications may be split into linked awards — plan proposals and budgets accordingly and monitor guidance on linked-award handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review: goals and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: "All peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) ... One Year Later: How Centralized NIH Peer Review is Strengthening Efficiency, Competition, and Transparency."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The consolidation of peer review into CSR is intended to improve efficiency, competition, and transparency of the review process. Applicants, reviewers, and institutions should be aware of process changes and initial effects reported by NIH as they may affect review assignment, timelines, and communications.
